text:
anya: Quick follow-up on pin/rollout metadata — sketching something lightweight to help client resolvers and ops. Proposal fields: `epoch`, `rollout_hint`, `affinity_score`, `soft_expiry`, `deprecation_signal`. Thoughts?

matt: high level — do we mean `deprecation_signal` as an advisory flag or a hard switch? e.g. do clients immediately fallback when set?

anya: advisory by default. we need a spectrum + strength value. hard kill should be separate (e.g. `hard_evict`). want clients to be able to prefer non-deprecated variants but still succeed. :thinking_face:

sarah: prefer soft path. say: `deprecation_signal: { level: "warning" | "critical", until: <ts>, reason: <short> }`. clients can treat `critical` as immediate failover. also want `soft_expiry` semantics for TTL-based eviction.

kevin: +1. to keep things concrete here's a tiny example for the rollout metadata we could include in the manifest: 

```json
{
  "epoch": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",
  "rollout_hint": "gradual-canary",
  "affinity_score": 0.82,
  "soft_expiry": "2025-08-01T00:00:00Z",
  "deprecation_signal": { "level": "warning", "until": "2025-09-01T00:00:00Z", "reason": "accuracy-regression" },
  "compatibility_matrix": ["kernel:v2","quantization:int8"],
  "labels": ["canary","low-cost"]
}
```

kevin: Notes: affinity_score is 0..1, used by smart routers for warm pins. keep `compatibility_matrix` as a list of capabilities (backwards-compatible).

matt: how should older clients behave if they see unknown fields? fail-open? ignore? we need explicit compatibility guarantees.

anya: guarantee: additive optional fields only. older clients ignore unknown keys (graceful) and respect `hard_evict` only if they understand it. we'll add a `schema_version` top-level to the manifest so we can evolve.

sarah: telemetry: include `rollout_epoch` and `affinity_score` in request traces so we can join evals -> regressions. also add `evaluation_set_id` opt field so we can tie quality alerts to specific rollouts.

kevin: one more thing — migration: operators can emit a `deprecation_broadcast` event when transitioning variants; clients listening on long-poll or SSE can pick up immediate signals rather than waiting for next manifest refresh.

anya: agreed. plan: I will open an RFC PR with: (1) schema draft, (2) migration plan for old clients, (3) minimal server-side semantics for `soft_expiry` vs `hard_evict`, (4) telemetry knobs. aiming to ship as opt-in v1 and make fields default-ignored by older runtimes.

matt: can you include exact invariants for `affinity_score`? e.g. non-negative, max 1, and tie-breaker rules when multiple pins apply.

anya: yes — will add: numeric 0..1, higher wins, tie-breaker: newer epoch preferred, then affinity, then lexical model id.

deploy-bot: lint: rollout-manifest-schema.json -> WARN: missing `schema_version` (line 1).

kevin: nice catch :sweat_smile: — schema_version should be required going forward.

sarah: also add a short human-readable `intent` field for runbooks (e.g., "reduce-costs", "canary-to-prod"). helps SRE when investigating.

anya: great. I'll draft and tag you all for review. TL;DR: additive, optional fields — `epoch`, `affinity_score`, `soft_expiry`, `deprecation_signal`, `compatibility_matrix`, `schema_version`, `intent`, `evaluation_set_id`. keep hard actions separate (`hard_evict`).

matt: :thumbsup:

kevin: one nit — prefer snake_case for JSON keys to match existing manifests.

anya: we'll standardize on snake_case. thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC link when ready.

sarah: thanks — this should make rollout telemetry + graceful migrations much easier. :sparkles:
